question: Every lane passage that states the round-20 context rule or a part of it; does X1 serving per-slot 2048 contradict it; which K05 frontier lines does the round advance.
tip_note: The assignment named tip 1fc41e346853afd98cbd7010af5db4e54dc877f7. `git diff --stat 1fc41e3 -- <all measured files>` was empty (exit 0), so the measured passage bytes are unchanged; c808ba0 adds amendment 3 and the committed C2 receipt.

x1_observed.provenance: committed by the L1 at 5ea4fc44; read by this seat, not produced by it; no server was launched by this seat

passages.quote: per-slot context is capped by --kv-unified-per-slot and the effective training context
passages.why: X1 /props 2048 is the capped per-slot value; the cap at training context 2048 holds.

passages.quote: Do not divide ctx by total_slots blindly: KV-unified and padding affect that relationship
passages.why: Still true: X1 would be wrong if props 2048 were divided by 4. The warning forbids that inference.

passages.quote: served n_ctx=256, training n_ctx_train=2048, and a GGUF declaration of 2048
passages.why: Different argv (-c 256, auto slots); no general rule is stated.

passages.quote: declared context versus meta.n_ctx_train, not props.n_ctx equality
passages.why: X1 props 2048 equals training 2048, but the rule is about which comparison is load-bearing, not that they must differ.

passages.quote: must not be computed as ctx / total_slots unconditionally
passages.why: Same caution as L2; X1 props/total coinciding with the per-slot value does not make the division safe in general.

passages.quote: single-model b11755 per-slot served context versus training-context metadata
passages.why: Scope statement only.

passages.quote: context size of a single slot, capped by --kv-unified-per-slot and by the training context of the model
passages.why: X1 per-slot 2048 equals the cap (training context 2048).

passages.quote: Props256/slots4 remain informational with no division.
passages.why: A dated statement about the -c 256 receipt; no general sizing formula.

passages.quote: props256 informational
passages.why: Dated evidence for the round-20 receipt; unaffected.

passages.quote: usable for historical comparison, not a new live endpoint sample
passages.why: No contradiction. This is the line the round advances: the committed receipt is a new live lane-owned sample.

passages.quote: n_ctx_seq = n_ctx if kv_unified else pad256(n_ctx // n_parallel)
passages.why: predict(0,2048,4,False,0) returns 512 (executed, exit 0); X1 observed 2048.

passages.quote: The model assumes that no --fit run lowered n_ctx
passages.why: Fit does not only lower: with unset -c and split KV it raises n_ctx to training x streams (fit.cpp:195-198, 266-273). X1 log candidates [2048, 8192, 8192].

passages.quote: otherwise GGML_PAD(n_ctx / n_seq_max, 256)
passages.why: The division is correct; the input differs (8192, not 2048). 8192/4 = 2048.
The --table run prints 512 for this tuple; X1 is that tuple and observed 2048.

passages.quote: /props is per-slot effective context, not ... an unconditional --ctx-size / --parallel quotient
passages.why: X1 props 2048 is the effective per-slot value.

passages.quote: n_ctx starts from explicit context size, or training context when zero
passages.why: True inside llama-context.cpp:219, false as a description of the server launch path with fit on: common/fit.cpp:271-272 rewrites n_ctx 0 to 8192 before the context is built.

passages.quote: split KV uses GGML_PAD(n_ctx / n_seq_max, 256)
passages.why: Formula holds for total 8192.

passages.quote: predicted=256 ... slots(naive ctx/slots=64)=no-match
passages.why: That receipt has -c 256; its replay is unaffected. The predictor that produced it is R1.

passages.quote: The effective per-slot size must reach D; -c 0 ... does not guarantee this when contexts are split across slots
passages.why: A non-guarantee, not a universal negation. X1 is a case where fit does reach D with split KV; the caveat should be scoped to --fit off (X3 512).

passages.quote: Argv -c is not S, because padding can raise it
passages.why: Still true; incomplete. It names padding as the only gap; fit is a second gap (X1 has no -c at all).

passages.quote: -fit ... may lower an unset context to no less than 4096
passages.why: Direction and floor are wrong for this case: fit raises unset n_ctx to training x streams (8192 observed) when memory allows; the 4096 floor is per-stream and only in the reduce branch (fit.cpp:268, 394).

passages.quote: Served per-slot n_ctx is not train/slots.
passages.why: X1 served 2048, train/slots 512; still unequal.

passages.quote: n_ctx 0 means 'use the train context'
passages.why: True at llama-context.cpp:219, false at the server parameter layer with fit on: fit sets training x streams. The landed entry dropped this sentence.

passages.quote: With kv_unified, n_ctx_seq = n_ctx; otherwise n_ctx / n_seq_max, padded to 256
passages.why: Same as R3.

passages.quote: every receipt has root ctx = 256, argv -c 256, and /props default_generation_settings.n_ctx = 256
passages.why: Explicitly not a scaling rule; X1 uses different argv.

passages.quote: every committed receipt and every kengaku capture has per-slot == total (O4/O6)
passages.why: X1 has per-slot 2048 and total pool 8192, so the 'unfalsifiable on this population' premise no longer holds.

passages.quote: props.n_ctx=256 is displayed as informational and is not compared to training context 2048
passages.why: Describes gguf-identity.py behavior, unchanged.

passages.quote: informational-only; not compared with training context
passages.why: Same as R17; also tools/gguf-identity.py:618.

passages.quote: Classification is based on served n_ctx versus training context
passages.why: X1 served 2048 versus training 2048 is 'within'; the advice also says neither ctx nor total_slots is multiplied or divided into that comparison.

passages.quote: context size of a single slot, capped by --kv-unified-per-slot and by the training context of the model
passages.why: Cap statement only.
